:::{#rem-mode-density}
#### A mode belongs to a density, not to a random variable

A [mode](#def-mode) is a property of a [density](#def-pdf) or [mass function](#def-pmf),
so "the mode of $X$" is shorthand for the mode of a chosen density of $X$.

Two [densities](#def-pdf) of the same [random variable](#def-random-variable)
can differ on a [set](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/sets.html#def-set) of [probability](probability-basics.qmd#def-probability) zero,
and then they can have different [modes](#def-mode).
A change of variables also moves the mode,
because the density of a transformed variable includes a Jacobian factor.

The [expectation](expectation.qmd#def-expectation) of $X$ is different:
it depends only on the [distribution](#def-cdf) of $X$,
so every density of $X$ gives the same value.

:::
